hook.line: Before an argument turns into a fight, someone has to say: wait, we're forgetting something. This phrase is how you say it.
hook.es: Hay que tener en cuenta el costo.
hook.en: You have to bear the cost in mind.

examples.es: Hay que tener en cuenta el costo.
examples.en: You have to bear the cost in mind.

examples.es: Ten en cuenta que cierran temprano.
examples.en: Bear in mind they close early. (to a friend)

examples.es: Tenemos que tener en cuenta a los vecinos.
examples.en: We have to take the neighbours into account.
Did you take the rent into account? (to a friend)

examples.es: No tuvieron en cuenta lo que dijo Hernando.
examples.en: They didn't take into account what Hernando said.
I take your opinion into account.

rule:
*Tener en cuenta* means to take something into account when you decide. Only *tener* changes: *tengo, tuviste, tuvieron*. The *en cuenta* part stays put.

What follows depends:

a thing, straight on: *el costo*
a person, with *a*: *a los vecinos*
a whole idea, with *que*: *Ten en cuenta que cierran temprano.*

*Ten* is the *tú* command of *tener*. *Hay que* is the all-purpose "you have to".
smallPrint: It is a set phrase: *tener en cuenta* always travels as one piece, and only *tener* takes the endings.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hay que tener ___ cuenta el costo.* (*en* or *con*)
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta el costo.
yourTurn.why: The set phrase is *tener en cuenta*, with *en*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: You have to take the rent into account.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta el arriendo.
accept: Hay que tomar en cuenta el arriendo.
yourTurn.why: *Hay que* plus the infinitive says what has to be done, and a thing follows directly.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: Bear in mind they close early.
yourTurn.answer: Ten en cuenta que cierran temprano.
yourTurn.why: *Ten* is the command to *tú*, and a whole idea needs *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We have to take the neighbours into account.
yourTurn.answer: Tenemos que tener en cuenta a los vecinos.
accept: Hay que tener en cuenta a los vecinos.
Tenemos que tomar en cuenta a los vecinos.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you take the rent into account?
yourTurn.why: Only *tener* changes: *tuviste* for *tú* in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a command to a friend: *Tienes en cuenta el costo.*
Make it past: *Tengo en cuenta tu opinión.*
Say we must take Hernando into account. He is a person, so add the little word.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que tener en cuenta a Hernando.
accept: Tenemos que tener en cuenta a Hernando.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que tener cuenta el costo.
pitfalls.right: Hay que tener en cuenta el costo.
pitfalls.why: The *en* is part of the set phrase, so it can't be dropped.

pitfalls.wrong: Hay que tener en cuenta Hernando.
pitfalls.right: Hay que tener en cuenta a Hernando.
pitfalls.why: When what you take into account is a person, it needs *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ten en cuenta de que cierran temprano.
pitfalls.right: Ten en cuenta que cierran temprano.
pitfalls.why: A whole idea follows with just *que*, with no *de*.

personal: Think of a decision you are making. Write one line with *hay que tener en cuenta* and one thing you would be wrong to forget, like the cost, the time or a person.
